Also: tests/test_paid_batch.py

failing_case: 30 Oct, master b55c82b9, podman image built 15 h earlier, `podman run ... bin/ci --quick` from a `--no-hardlinks` clone: 12 failing test batches. Seen: test_paid_batch ("paid-cost: the default branch cannot be told": the clone has no default branch), test_rules_gate_isolation (a ResourceWarning turns into a failure), test_gate_slots test_t4_a_gate_already_waiting_reclaims_* hung 10 min (the image has no lsof: not verified). lsof present in the image or the slot reclaim not needing it on Linux.
reason: tests/test_quick_gate_image.py:92 (Containerfile has no identity env) and the gate/sync test fixes; the identity test and step tests fail at ddea7ab8 and pass at head. The image run is the fixer's report (clean image exit 0), not seen by me.

details: CONFIRMED by grep. The What line is the item's promise and "red again" is the second occurrence of the same kind of failure:
principle 6 (cause, not symptom: fix the rule behind it, not one example) asks for the guard that keeps it green, which the
item itself names. Without it the remote/Linux gate host the owner is now asking about (ai.amidman.com) has no guarantee the
gate means the same thing there. The item allows either the gate or a paid step; a paid step on the default branch after a
wave is the cheap one (one image run per wave, ~15-20 min of a Linux/podman machine). Size: 45 agent minutes.
evidence: git grep -n -i "podman\|Containerfile\|clean-gate" -- bin lib tests plugins templates docs/*.md  -> (no output)
relay queue show the-quick-gate-is-red-again-in-a-clean-linux-ima -> What: "... and keep it green (the gate or a paid step runs it)."
fixer report: "DONE: bin/ci --quick exit 0 in rebuilt clean image" (no step added, no log kept)
failing_case: The item's What: "Make bin/ci --quick green in the clean image ... and keep it green (the gate or a paid step runs it)."
At ddea7ab8, `git grep -i 'podman|Containerfile|clean-gate' -- bin lib tests plugins templates` finds nothing: no gate step,
paid step or test builds the image or runs the recipe. The recipe was closed green on 29 Oct (the-quick-gate-is-red-in-a-clean-
linux-container) and was red again on 30 Oct (b55c82b9, 12 failing batches) with nobody noticing until a design measured it.
After this change the same happens: a test that relies on macOS (lsof name form, git identity guessing, origin/HEAD) lands green
on the Mac gate and turns the image red silently. Should be: a paid step (or a gate step) that builds the image and runs the recipe
on the head and is red when it is.
fix_hint: Add a paid-run step (where the paid run lists its steps) that builds container/Containerfile with podman, clones the head into
the image as the comment's recipe does, runs bin/ci --quick with a time bound, and keeps the log; red on a non-zero exit,
"skipped: no podman" when podman is absent. A test of the step's command list with a fake podman.
pass_cases: 1. A paid run (or the gate, whichever the fix picks) on a head whose quick gate is green in the image: the step runs
`podman build` + the Containerfile recipe and reports green with the image run's own log (head sha, exit 0).
2. The same step on a head with a test that fails only on Linux (e.g. assert sys.platform == "darwin"): the step is red and names the test.
3. A machine without podman: the step says it was skipped and why, not green.
4. This Mac's quick gate keeps its current duration (the image run is not added to every quick gate unless that is the choice made).
reason: tests/test_quick_gate_image.py:69-100 (recipe order podman build/clone/checkout/run, red image run makes the step red and stops before evals, green shows time, no podman is red). lib/relay_ci.py runs the step only when not quick. Fails at ddea7ab8, passes at head.
findings.summary: the item's 'and keep it green (the gate or a paid step runs it)' is not built: nothing runs the clean-image recipe, so it can go red a third time unseen

details: CONFIRMED that git refuses in the image without the variables (reproduced); PLAUSIBLE which tests depended on it: the fixer did
not name them (heuristic grep candidates: tests/test_gate_slots.py, tests/test_lanes_state.py, tests/test_queue_close.py, and
tests whose fixtures set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null without an author). Principle 6: the image is changed to fit the tests'
macOS assumption instead of fixing the assumption, and the item's Why is that a Linux gate must mean the same thing; the owner
is now asking to run gates on a Linux VPS. Size: 30 agent minutes.
evidence: podman run --rm relay-clean-gate sh -c 'unset GIT_AUTHOR_NAME GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL GIT_COMMITTER_NAME GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL; export HOME=/tmp/h; ... git init -q && git commit -q --allow-empty -m x'
-> fatal: unable to auto-detect email address (got 'dev@7cc4df9b5a7e.(none)')  exit=128
container/Containerfile:15-16 comment: "tests run git with a HOME of their own (no ~/.gitconfig): the author has to come from the environment, as macOS guesses it from the user"
failing_case: In the image without the new ENV line: HOME=/tmp/h git init && git commit --allow-empty -m x ->
"fatal: unable to auto-detect email address (got 'dev@7cc4df9b5a7e.(none)')", exit 128. The fixer's own comment says some tests
"run git with a HOME of their own (no ~/.gitconfig)" and pass on macOS only because macOS guesses an identity. The image now
sets the identity in its environment, so those tests are green in the image but still fail on any Linux machine or container that
runs bin/ci --quick without that variable and with a hostname lacking a domain (a podman/CI container, many VPS setups).
Should be: each such test gives its git calls an identity itself (as tests/test_gate.py GIT_ENV and tests/test_hook_merge.py do),
and the image needs no identity variable.
fix_hint: Run the quick gate in the image once without the ENV line, list the failing tests, give their fixtures an identity
(GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* in the env they pass, or -c user.name/-c user.email), then drop the ENV line.
pass_cases: 1. The clean image with the ENV GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* line removed: bin/ci --quick exits 0.
2. Each test the ENV line was covering (the fixer names them) passes with env -u GIT_AUTHOR_NAME -u GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL
-u GIT_COMMITTER_NAME -u GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL HOME=<empty temp> on Linux.
3. This Mac's quick gate stays green.
reason: tests/test_quick_gate_image.py:123 (no GIT_AUTHOR/GIT_COMMITTER in container/Containerfile), plus in-process identity in tests/test_gate.py, test_verdict.py, test_gate_stops.py; fails at ddea7ab8, passes at head.
findings.summary: GIT_AUTHOR/COMMITTER env in the image hides tests that commit with no identity; on a Linux host whose hostname has no domain they fail

details: CONFIRMED by reading: os.path.join(root, "bin", "relay") with root = a git clone of ROOT. The gate runs on a committed head, so
the gate result is right; the gap is the worker's loop before a commit. Size: 15 agent minutes.
evidence: tests/test_paid_batch.py:179-183 clone ROOT -> root; checkout -B master HEAD; run python3 root/bin/relay sync
failing_case: A worker edits bin/relay's sync wait (or bin/paid-cost due) in the worktree and runs pytest tests/test_paid_batch.py before
committing: run_sync clones ROOT (committed objects only) and runs <clone>/bin/relay, so the test checks the old committed code
and passes with the new behaviour disabled or broken. Each of the 2 calls also clones the whole repository (measured 5.1 s,
76 MB on this Mac). Should be: the code under test is the working tree's; only the git data needs a master branch.
fix_hint: Keep running ROOT/bin/relay and give the default branch to git only: e.g. clone with --shared --no-checkout (or a bare clone) for
the repo paid-cost reads, if sync takes the repo from RELAY_ROOT, or set a refs/heads/master in a temp GIT_DIR alternate; or
create refs/heads/master in ROOT only when it is missing and remove it in cleanup.
pass_cases: 1. An uncommitted edit that removes the "waits for a green paid run" refusal: test_sync_refuses_with_the_due_list_and_writes_nothing fails.
2. A fresh clone of a detached commit (the image recipe): both SyncWaits tests pass.
3. This worktree with master present: both pass.
reason: tests/test_quick_gate_image.py:21 and :36 (run_sync runs this checkout's bin/relay, clones nothing, leaves no master it made); both pass at head.
findings.summary: run_sync runs bin/relay from a clone of HEAD, so an uncommitted change to sync or paid-cost is not what this test exercises, and each call clones the repo (5 s)

details: CONFIRMED by reading lib/relay_gate.py:200-203 and lib/relay_procs.py:91-96. Outside: neither file is touched by this change;
the change makes lsof present in the image and listed in deps.toml, which meets the item's pass case but leaves the silent unbounded
wait on any machine that lacks it. Size: 30 agent minutes.
evidence: lib/relay_procs.py:93 subprocess.run(["lsof", "-t", "--", path]) ... except (OSError, ...): return None
lib/relay_gate.py:201-203 holders = relay_procs.holders_of(path); if not holders: return False
failing_case: A Linux machine without lsof (the state of the image before this change; any Debian/Ubuntu slim host): a gate's process dies
while its command keeps relay-gate.lock open; the next relay gate in that worktree calls take_worktree_lock -> reclaim ->
relay_procs.holders_of returns None (lsof not found) -> reclaim returns False -> the loop polls forever with only
"gate: waiting for the gate already running in this worktree (pid N has ended; ...)". The item saw this as a 10-minute hang of
test_gate_slots test_t4_a_gate_already_waiting_reclaims_*. Should be: on Linux find holders through /proc/*/fd (as read_cwds
already uses /proc), or say once "cannot tell who holds <lock>: lsof is missing (relay doctor)".
fix_hint: holders_of: on Linux read /proc/<pid>/fd links (no lsof); elsewhere, when lsof is missing, return None and have
take_worktree_lock print one line naming lsof and relay doctor.
pass_cases: 1. PATH without lsof on Linux, a dead gate pid and its group holding the lock: the waiting gate reclaims (via /proc) or prints the lsof line once.
2. lsof present: the reclaim works as today (test_gate_slots t4 tests pass).
3. A live holder: the gate waits, as today.
reason: tests/test_gate_slots.py LsofCannotRun (line ~465): one line naming lsof and relay doctor when holders_of is None; fails at ddea7ab8, passes at head. The wait still does not end without lsof (the line says to stop the group by hand), which the review's pass case 1 accepts.
findings.summary: when lsof cannot run, the wait for a dead gate's worktree lock never ends and never says lsof is missing
